analysis.title: EPAM Systems Inc. (EPAM): Narrowed outlook with strong margin performance; increases capital allocation commitment
key_insights: GS expects EPAM stock to trade higher after the company announced a larger buyback authorization and a near-term accelerated share repurchase, which GS says should help investors gain confidence in the valuation at current levels.
GS maintains a Neutral rating. It expects near-term pressure to persist but sees potential for longer-term upside once execution improves and discretionary spending stabilizes.
GS says EPAM's fundamentals appear to have stabilized after earlier execution challenges and early traction with large client deals.
For the stock to work from current levels, GS says EPAM needs a re-acceleration in topline growth together with gross margin expansion.

EPAM plans a $500mn accelerated share repurchase over the next week, funded with cash on hand and its existing credit facility. The Board added a $1.5bn repurchase authorization, supporting a return of at least 50% of free cash flow to shareholders from 2027 through 2029.
Management described demand as relatively stable versus last quarter. EPAM has signed three large transformational client deals, in line with its stated goals.
By vertical, EPAM sees continued strength in Financial Services and Life Sciences/Healthcare. It sees headwinds in Consumer Goods/Retail/Travel, Software/Hi-Tech and Business Information/Media.

Management expects an improving growth rate in 2027, with sequential growth in 1H as new large deals ramp. It guides 2027 operating margin to 15%-16%, with gross margin flat to modestly lower on a smaller R&D credit benefit.
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin was 32.8% against the Street at 32.1% and GS at 31.8%. Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.7% against the Street at 16.1% and GS at 16.2%.
AI-native revenue was over $185mn in 3Q26, up from $160mn in 2Q26. Management raised its 2026 AI-native revenue target to $650mn from $600mn.
GS views the results as neutral for its IT Services coverage, given relatively in-line revenue and outlook.

GS raised its 12-month price target to $140 from $100, on 9X (up from 7X on higher peer multiples) its one-year forward earnings estimate. The stock closed at $137.36 on 4 Nov 2026 per the disclosure appendix.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $140 from $100 on a 9X forward P/E (up from 7X on higher peer multiples). Rating stays Neutral, with near-term pressure expected to persist.

sector_views.rationale: GS views EPAM's results as neutral for its IT Services coverage given relatively in-line revenue results and outlook.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 revenue (reported): $1.426bn vs GS estimate $1.423bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $1.419bn. Y/Y growth +2.3%.
3Q26 non-GAAP EPS from continuing operations (reported): $3.51 vs GS estimate $3.43 and Street $3.40. Y/Y +14.0%.
3Q26 non-GAAP gross margin (reported): 32.8% vs GS estimate 31.8% and Street 32.1%. Non-GAAP operating margin (reported): 16.7% vs GS 16.2% and Street 16.1%.

2026 revenue guidance narrowed to 3.5%-3.7% growth (prior 3.2%-4.2%), or $5.65-$5.66bn. GS estimate was $5.672bn and Street $5.655bn. Organic constant-currency growth is 2.5%-2.7% (prior 2.0%-3.0%) with a positive 1.0% FX impact.
4Q26 revenue guidance (company): $1.405-$1.420bn, about 1.1% organic constant-currency growth at the midpoint. GS estimate was $1.435bn and Street $1.422bn.
2026 adjusted operating margin guidance (company): 15.9%-16.1%, vs GS and Street at 15.8%.
2026 adjusted EPS guidance (company) raised to $13.23-$13.31 from $13.08-$13.24 prior. GS estimate was $13.20 and Street $13.14.

GS estimate changes: 2026/27/28 EPS now $13.23/$14.40/$16.60 from $13.20/$14.00/$15.00, reflecting modest changes to gross margin and buyback assumptions. 2026/27/28 revenue is $5,657mn/$5,846mn/$6,158mn.

GS 2027 non-GAAP operating margin estimate falls to 15.6% from 16.1%, and the 2028 estimate to 15.7% from 16.3%. GS expects modest gross margin pressure from lower R&D credit benefit and large-deal conversion in 2027.
risk_factors: Upside risks: earlier-than-expected recovery in discretionary IT spending, increased demand for AI-related projects, stronger-than-expected deal conversion.
Downside risks: further demand slowdown, dilutive M&A, increased geopolitical tensions.
Ongoing headwinds in discretionary spending, and lower R&D credit benefit weighing on gross margin.

tension_points.bull_case: The buyback ($500mn ASR plus $1.5bn authorization) should build confidence in valuation. Three large deals signed, margins beat, AI-native revenue is growing, and management expects growth to improve in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Discretionary spending headwinds persist, near-term pressure is likely, and GS expects modest gross margin pressure in 2027 from lower R&D credits. GS's $140 target implies a base case of -15.1% from its $165 reference in the exhibit, and its bear case is $89.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to re-accelerate topline growth together with gross margin expansion, which GS says the stock needs to work from current levels.
